points: Hashem tells Yirmiyahu not to marry or have children "in this place." Some say only in Anasos, his hostile town. The Abarbanel says a navi can be told to set aside a mitzvah for a time, like Eliyahu on Har HaCarmel.
It also shows how young he was. He's also told not to go to shiva houses or weddings, which everyone in a small town went to.
The point is for people to ask why. The answer: so many will die that there will be no mourning and no weddings. A visible act teaches more than words.

Why does Yirmiyahu repeat himself so much? Because his message is shocking: after Yoshiyahu's revival, they look religious on the outside but are still idolatrous inside. Outward observance isn't enough.
A promise of comfort: one day we'll speak of Hashem who brought us out of all the lands of exile, and it will overshadow Yetzias Mitzrayim. We're starting to see it now.
